question_type: Midpoint ('Fisher Ideal symmetric') growth rate between two monthly yields from Table AY-1, vintage pinned to FY1982-end issues; answer is a unitless rate to 3 decimals

opus_path.decision: Parsed series = monthly average yield of long-term Treasury bonds (AY-1), months Aug 1981 (base) and Aug 1982, vintage = FY1982 end (Sep/Oct 1982 issues), output = one number to 3 dp; flagged the formula name as ambiguous
Listed issues around FY1982 end, chose the Oct 1982 issue as the first issue after FY end
Read AY-1 in treasury_bulletin_1982_10.txt; identified the 4th year panel as 1981/1982 via panel year-label rows
Took the 'Treasury bonds 1/' column (not the adjacent 'New Aa corporate bonds' despite the word 'new'); stripped the '5/' footnote prefix using the footnote text
Cross-vintage check over 1982_09, 1982_11, 1983_03, 1983_06: all FY1982-era printings identical; 1983 issues redefine the series (20-yr constant maturity), so rejected by the vintage pin
Fisher ideal index of one series collapses to the ratio; applied the symmetric (midpoint) growth 2(F-1)/(F+1); logged simple, log and geometric-mean alternatives
Reported the rate as a decimal fraction, explicitly rejecting the percent (x100) form because '(in percent)' qualifies the input yields and the answer clause names no percent
Adversarial reviewer re-opened cells, recomputed, and named decimal-vs-percent as the only residual risk

opus_key_moves: Treated '(in percent)' as a property of the input yields and the answer clause ('single numeric value rounded to three decimal places') as the output spec, so committed the bare fraction and wrote the percent form down only as a rejected alternative
Resolved the unfamiliar formula name quickly by reduction (Fisher index of one series = ratio) and logged the alternatives instead of searching the corpus for a definition
Checked all FY1982-era printings plus the 1983 redefinition, so the vintage question was closed in one step

remedies.intervention: Commit-time answer-scale check: extract the answer clause of the question (e.g. 'report your answer as ...'); if it contains no 'percent'/'%' and the committed number equals 100x the last printed computed value, reject and ask for the bare value (or for an explicit quote of the question span that makes the answer a percent).
remedies.why: The actor had the unscaled value in its own reasoning ([34]) and chose x100 by prior at [53]; a check at the exact decision point with a deterministic rule removes the prior. Risk: some questions do want percent without saying so in the answer clause.

remedies.intervention: Repeated-command guard: after 3 identical commands with identical output, block the command and force a 'decide and commit' turn with the current candidate.
remedies.why: 165 identical grep runs [52]-[380] and a compaction; the guard would have saved ~1800 s and ~25M tokens (it would not by itself fix the scale error).

remedies.intervention: Convention: a unit phrase attached to the inputs ('yield (in percent)') does not make a derived growth rate a percent; growth/change rates are committed as decimal fractions unless the answer clause says percent.
remedies.why: The prompt arm had essentially this text (L-midpoint-percent-change) and still chose x100 at [38]; text alone is weak for this actor.

right_arms_note: No arm was right. All three found the correct AY-1 Treasury-bond cells in FY1982-end issues and the midpoint formula; all three reported the x100 form. The difference from Opus is only the output-scale decision.
text_vs_mechanism: Text alone is unlikely to fix this: the prompt arm had a verified lesson stating that unit phrases describe the inputs and that the bare ratio is committed unless the question says percent, weighed both forms at [38], and still chose x100 by prior. A commit-time scale check (plus a loop guard for the none/cards arms' thrash) is the more reliable fix.
notes: Uniform failure across arms points to a strong actor prior ('growth rate => percent') that is triggered by any 'percent' token in the question. Two of three arms also lost most of their budget to identical-command loops while deliberating (formula definition in none, vintage in cards) with no new information arriving; the corpus contains no definition of the formula name, so corpus search for it is wasted effort. The prompt learner added a specific lesson for this question after the postmortem, so a re-run could test whether question-specific text transfers.
